My experience at this house with the staff over a weekend was quite negative, and frankly, I wouldn't recommend it.

From the moment we arrived, the owners were very strict about everything. They even went so far as to count the towels and check that absolutely everything was in place "centimeter by centimeter," implying that if it wasn't, they might not return our deposit.

Furthermore, we had several significant problems during our stay. We were without electricity for approximately three hours, from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM, and the supposed electrician didn't arrive until 12:30 AM. Upon arriving at the house, we also discovered that there was no water anywhere, so we had to try to resolve both the electrical and plumbing issues ourselves. The water technician never even showed up.

In short, we felt that for the price and the conditions, we expected much more. The problems we encountered made the weekend quite uncomfortable, and we had to deal with issues that weren't our responsibility.

On the plus side, there was a rather persistent cat, although I personally loved it. 🐈‍⬛

Because of everything that happened, I wouldn't recommend this accommodation.

one_star_reviews.text:
Gym with old but good machines, where you can train well. It is a fairly neglected gym and, when the instructor is there, he is usually chatting instead of advising people who are doing the exercises wrong or disinfecting the benches, as they do in other gyms.

The changing rooms are also usually wet, with puddles of water, and on occasion there have been cockroaches. In this aspect, the cleaning and maintenance could be much improved.

It is a shame, because it is a good place to train and has a lot of potential, but a few years ago there was better staff and more attention and care was noticed for the facilities and for the users. With a little more maintenance, cleaning and customer service, it could be a much better gym.

one_star_reviews.text:
🚨 A FAMILY WITH TWO YOUNG CHILDREN LEFT STRANDED AT ALGECIRAS PORT 🚨

We booked and paid for a car in advance with **Enterprise Alquiler de Coches y Furgonetas – Algeciras** through Booking.com. When we arrived at the Algeciras agency at around 4 p.m., they refused to give us the vehicle, claiming that it should have been collected before 1 p.m.

But the most shocking part was what happened next: they offered us NO alternative car, NO assistance and NO solution whatsoever.

At 5 p.m., we were simply left stranded at the port with two very young children, all our luggage, no car and no way to reach our accommodation in Torremolinos. We felt completely abandoned in an unfamiliar place, despite having booked and paid in advance.

Our only option was to pay for an extremely expensive taxi from Algeciras to Torremolinos. Instead of acknowledging what happened, Booking.com is now hiding behind the term “no-show” — even though we physically arrived at the agency and tried to collect our prepaid vehicle.

How can a major international company consider it acceptable to leave a family with small children stranded without offering even the slightest assistance?

This was not a minor inconvenience. It was an extremely stressful and distressing situation that left our family feeling vulnerable and completely unsupported.

We demand a full refund, reimbursement of our additional transport costs and an immediate investigation into how this was handled.

Please share this so that other families know how customers can be treated by **Enterprise Alquiler de Coches y Furgonetas – Algeciras** and Booking.com.

@Enterprise @Bookingcom — take responsibility and resolve this immediately.

one_star_reviews.text:
On Friday, I took a kitten I'd rescued from the street to the vet for deworming. He was malnourished and riddled with parasites. The vet who examined him prescribed an antiparasitic that almost killed him, literally. She seemed to prioritize the kitten's age over his weight when determining the dosage. She prescribed five doses to be administered over five consecutive days. The kitten, who wasn't even a month and a half old, started having terrible diarrhea on Saturday, and on Sunday, he had diarrhea and vomiting. I brought him back to Madrid because I'd found him a home. On the way to Madrid, in the car, the kitten began showing neurological signs (a fixed stare with no response to stimuli, stiff legs, and abnormal head movements). Within minutes, he was unresponsive, turning cyanotic, with pauses in breathing, squinting eyes, no menace reflex, and completely hypotonic. We had to find an emergency vet because the kitten was literally dying. He came into the emergency room Sunday afternoon diagnosed with a hypoglycemic coma. They told me he was dehydrated due to vomiting and diarrhea caused by the Panacur, which is very strong in such weak animals and shouldn't be administered. The cat was given glucose boluses for over two hours because even the glucometer wouldn't register his blood sugar level, and he had to be hospitalized. He was discharged yesterday, and thankfully, "Huevito" is much better now.

I don't know the name of the veterinarian who saw him, but now, thinking about it rationally, I remember her having doubts during the consultation and making comments that make me think she might not even have a veterinary degree. With something as simple as deworming a cat, she practically sent him packing.
Absolutely never again. Even if I find 80 stray cats, they'll never set foot in that vet's office again.

one_star_reviews.text: My experience there was "shameful." The reviews weren't good, but I decided to take a couple of machines in: a Bosch angle grinder that had stopped working and a Makita wood chipper that needed a new chuck because it had broken. Simple repairs on machines they work on, so I decided to take them in and not overthink it. I took them in and explained the situation. They told me they'd call me the next day or the day after with a quote, so far so good. About 7 or 8 days passed, and they sent me the quote. For the Bosch angle grinder, they said they'd have to replace practically all the internal components, which is illogical because that's taking the easy way out and doesn't make sense. So I told them I wasn't interested in fixing it, and if it took them a week to give me a quote, I didn't want to wait a month to have all the components replaced. They also gave me a quote for the chuck for the wood chipper, and even though it was expensive, I told them it was worth it just to avoid the hassle. A week goes by and I ask them what's wrong. They tell me the supplier is out of stock and that they'll file a claim... They offer no solutions, and I don't understand what's wrong with a drill chuck... Three weeks later, I ask again and still haven't received a response. So, after more than a month with my tools at this workshop, I decide to pick them up and never set foot in there again. Here's another surprise, which, along with everything else, is why I'm writing this review. I pick up the grinder without any problem, exactly as I gave it to them, but they tell me the Bosch angle grinder is disassembled. From the time I told them I wasn't getting it fixed until that point, approximately 21 days had passed. They didn't even bother to put it back the way it was, so I had to take the disassembled grinder home in a box. I wouldn't take even the simplest thing to them. I don't know why this place is still open. It's simply shameful service. If you see this review, look elsewhere. You don't want to wait more than a month for something they might not even fix. In my case, I left with my tools in worse condition than when I brought them in.

*EDITED AFTER RESPONSE*
No one disputes that someone can make a mistake; we all know we're human. But making a mistake is one thing, and taking seedlings that someone is going to buy without checking if they're in good condition or counting them is another.
I have the invoice in front of me right now. I have to say, it seems quite strange to me that you issue invoices directly as paid in cash and then modify them yourselves when I have to submit the same invoice (I'll have to consult my accountant about this) because it could harm me if I submit the invoice and it doesn't match yours. In my business experience, I have NEVER encountered a situation like this from any establishment. Also, regarding the invoice, it's odd that I can't even verify how many seedlings I bought or what varieties (I can understand the second point, but not the quantity). There aren't even product codes to verify what was purchased or the price. I can't go and demand an invoice if the quantities I bought aren't even listed. The address listed is also incorrect. I gave the saleswoman my ID directly to copy it; it only shows the street address. This reflects a lack of concern on her part.
We understand that businesses are busy, especially in the summer, but what we cannot accept is being left alone in the store for 10 minutes, being sold dead seedlings because they haven't checked them, receiving fewer seedlings than necessary because they take the root ball and remove it without counting them, and being told that you're providing a different invoice that I don't have and wouldn't have if I hadn't left this comment.
One mistake is one thing, but the series of errors in this case is another. This isn't an isolated incident, as you have other reviews saying the same thing about the quantity and quality of the seedlings.
Finally, this is the first time I've bought from you as a professional, and I'm sorry to say it will also be the last. I will contact you to request the correct invoice by email, as I'm not going to waste my precious time going there to discuss something when I won't be buying again, especially since you're making excuses for poor service instead of apologizing and offering to resolve the invoice issue.

A very bad experience. We went to buy seedlings for our garden, and when we took them out, the saleswoman neither counted them nor checked their condition. To the point that when we planted them, several were dead and a few were missing.

We also requested an invoice and paid by card, but the invoice shows the payment as cash.

Considering we came based on a friend's recommendation, we were very disappointed, and the saleswoman's service left much to be desired.

one_star_reviews.text:
I stayed from August 16th to 23rd at Manuel Comellas, paying around €860, and the experience was quite awful.

My main complaint is that none of the issues shown in the attached photos were disclosed before booking. The photos in the listing were completely different.

The apartment was very run down: dampness, a sewage smell, a stained sofa, general dirt, creaking beds, dirty cutlery, and broken, filthy pans. I understand that accommodation can be basic, but at that price, the bare minimum is cleanliness and maintenance. Not to mention that a pan costs €20 anywhere else.

The worst part was the handling of the issue. When we complained, the company didn't offer us any equivalent alternative. They claim they offered us other accommodation, but it was Airbnb who suggested a hotel, which obviously isn't a substitute for an apartment and didn't cover the additional costs.

Airbnb, within reason, responded much better. The management company simply passed the buck and even tried to shift the official complaint onto the owner, even though they are the ones managing the accommodation.

I would never book anything managed by this company again.

EDIT: RESPONSE TO THE OWNER

-There wasn't a single pan in good condition.

-The dampness, even though the insurance company is coming to inspect it, hadn't been fixed or reported before we booked. Had we known, we obviously wouldn't have rented.

-The bed in the left-hand room creaks and is impossible to sleep on, no matter what you say.

-We have so little grounds for complaint that Airbnb refunded us half of the reservation.

Conclusion: You upload photos to a listing that don't reflect reality, and the proof is there.

one_star_reviews.text:
The impossible burger.

I didn’t think it was possible to create a burger that was completely devoid of taste or substance. But this was frankly embarrassing.  When my ‘queens’ burger arrived I thought it was a joke.
No taste.
No structure.
One piece of dry mostly fat bacon.

It was minced meat that crumbled in my hand and proved difficult to eat - which after tasting was perhaps a blessing.
There was no difference between my partners ‘well done’ vs my ‘medium rare’ (apart from the toothpick flag that stated well done on hers). Both looked and tasted like they had been boiled and pressed together.

Even the salad had no taste which considering it had red onion and tomato, I could not understand.

And the ‘cheddar’ cheese… oh dear. Maybe it had been microwaved.

I understand running a profitable restaurant is hard and really want them to succeed, but if the owners and staff don’t care and produce food of such a low level and thus overpriced I have little sympathy for them.

Best part of the burger? The lettuce.

one_star_reviews.text: As a bank branch, they function well. My low rating stems from the insurance I have with them, Caser. Since the beginning of April, I've been suffering from the great incompetence with which this insurance company operates. At the beginning of April, I discovered that my roof had tiles lifted due to a storm a few days prior. I filed a claim with the insurance company, as the wind exceeded the threshold specified in the policy. From then on, it was an ordeal to get the damage repaired. I received calls day after day, from the adjuster to the claims handler, but nobody knew when the roof would be repaired. Days passed, and every time it rained, I had damage and flooding inside the house. At the beginning of May, they informed me that they would come to repair the roof on June 1st. Fifty days after the damage, the repair company finished on June 18th, and with the following rains, I had new leaks. Here's the kicker... First, once the repair work was finished, the repair company, Caser, told me they wouldn't cover the water damage inside (even though they had promised to repair it) because of the delay in coming to do the repairs, nor would they cover the new leaks. This is a rip-off of the insured. By the way, the company they sent to repair the roof is called INSER. I rejected that repair company because of how shoddy their work is, even though they charged Caser €10,000 for the repairs. In conclusion, based on my personal experience, I won't take out any insurance with Caser through Ibercaja, even though the broker at this branch did everything possible. Caser didn't pay any attention to him, so I don't know what the point is (I decided to go to this branch because I had someone to talk to personally). I'd rather go with an online insurer that has cheaper insurance. In the end, I've put these matters in the hands of my lawyer.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would never buy or sell with them again.

In our case, it was a double transaction: buying one house and selling another. Honestly, I wouldn't do it again for anything.
There was a serious lack of professionalism throughout the entire process. Many lies were exposed when we spoke with the seller of the house we were buying and with potential buyers of the house we were selling.
It was a months-long process, and I regretted contacting them many times. I finally sold my house, and Álvaro, the person "in charge" of the sale, didn't even show up for the signing. I put "in charge" in quotes because the sale was thanks to Esmeralda. Álvaro only made promises, but when it came down to it, he delivered nothing.

And the purchase went through thanks to an external party who resolved a problem for us at the last minute. Christine, after having the house for months, didn't even realize it had a lien and that, in its current state, it couldn't be sold. Besides having to constantly request the documentation the notaries required for the deeds.

It's appalling what they charge for the work they do.
In short, a process riddled with lies and blunders.
They lack experience and, above all, honesty with clients; otherwise, they should at least learn to lie so we don't catch them.
I'll stick with Esmeralda, who is undoubtedly far superior to the rest. She's professional, friendly, keeps her word, and makes sure everything is done smoothly and on time.

Also, I just got a coke can without glass and ice. The service is hilariously unprofessional and the food doesn't make up for it at all. I hope this can help and lead to some improvement! The whole inside and facade feel cold and industrialised like a modern McDonald's or similar. It's not a comfy place for sure. All that aside, it's understandable that the staff are also just humans with bad days, but sadly people pay money here and want to be treated with respect.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience, particularly regarding the handling of my security deposit.

I rented a room in Madrid managed by Rookie in Town for five months. Unfortunately, my experience after moving out has been extremely disappointing.
My security deposit was €399, but I received only €45.65 back. The remaining amount was deducted for various alleged damages, repairs, cleaning and utilities.
What concerns me most is that I was charged for repairing damage to the bathroom ceiling even though I have dated photo and video evidence from my check-in showing that the ceiling was already damaged when I moved in.
I was also charged for alleged “misuse” involving a bed base and the washing machine, as well as for another repair. I formally disputed these deductions and asked Rookie in Town to provide sufficient evidence supporting the allegation of misuse. In my view, the documentation I received did not adequately establish this.
I also disputed their utility calculation. My contract required monthly provisional utility payments, and I kept the corresponding payment records.
I made several attempts to resolve the matter directly with Rookie in Town and submitted my objections in writing. Unfortunately, despite extensive correspondence, we were unable to reach a satisfactory resolution.
I also contacted Spacest, the platform through which I originally booked the accommodation, and asked them for assistance with the dispute. Unfortunately, I was unable to obtain a satisfactory resolution through Spacest either. I was ultimately instructed to contact Rookie in Town again using a different email address, despite the fact that I had already been in extensive written correspondence with Rookie in Town regarding the same dispute. Based on my experience with this case, I therefore cannot recommend Spacest either.
As the matter remained unresolved, I eventually had to pursue it legally myself and submit my claim and supporting evidence to the competent court in Madrid.
I have retained all relevant documentation, including the rental contract, payment records, invoices, emails, photographs and check-in/check-out evidence.
Based on my personal experience, I cannot recommend Rookie in Town. I would strongly advise other tenants, especially international students, to take detailed photos and videos when moving in and out, keep all payment records and carefully document every communication concerning the security deposit.

You should update your Google profile's hours when you decide to close earlier than usual. If you publicly state that the establishment closes at 2:00 PM, it's understandable that customers travel there trusting that information.

Today I went there specifically to arrange a SEUR package. I arrived at 1:40 PM, and according to the hours published on Google, there were still 20 minutes until closing time. However, upon arrival, I found the establishment seemingly closed and a sign on the door indicating that today, Friday, they were closing at 1:30 PM. This change in hours was not reflected on Google.

To make matters worse, I noticed that there was someone inside assisting a customer, also with a package. Despite having traveled there based on the hours you yourselves have published, I was simply told that you were closed and that I would have to return on Monday.

I find this customer service extremely poor. If the opening hours are exceptionally changed, the least they can do is update them on public channels to prevent people from wasting their time traveling to the establishment. And since I was still inside helping another customer, I think they could have at least had the courtesy to serve me as well, especially considering that my presence there was precisely due to their incorrect opening hours information. As a result, I now have to wait all weekend to pick up my package.

I can't comment on other aspects of the establishment, but my first experience was frankly bad and demonstrates a clear lack of care in both the information they provide to the public and the customer service they offer.

To make matters worse, my experience with SEUR is another issue: the package ended up at this collection point because they supposedly couldn't deliver it to my home, which is hard to believe, since I have 24/7 package delivery.

Between a delivery that apparently wasn't even attempted properly and an official SEUR location that publishes a schedule it then fails to meet or update, the experience was terrible for both parties.

I will certainly avoid both this establishment and SEUR whenever possible.
